--- title: "Simulation Based Estimation of Sampling Bias" jupyter: python3 fig-dpi: 300 bibliography: references.bib --- ```{=html} ``` # Data and models **Field.** GLORYS12V1 reanalysis on its native $1/12^\circ$ grid. OHC is the $0$–$2000$ m depth integral of potential temperature against constant $c_p\rho$ (`code/ohc.py`), evaluated daily over 2010–2019. Cells enter the analysis only where $\mathrm{deptho} > 2000$ m *and* the integral is defined at every level. **Mean field.** OHC is split as $\mathrm{OHC} = \hat m + \tilde Z$ into a smooth climatological mean field $\hat m$, fitted once across $1995$–$2019$, and the residual anomaly field $\tilde Z$. $\hat m$ is a per-cell OLS on a quadratic trend plus annual and semiannual harmonics, fit against the GLORYS *monthly* record with each basis function averaged over its month to match the monthly-mean response, then evaluated pointwise per day. @sec-meanfield gives the estimator and summarizes what it leaves. **Advection.** OceanParcels, park depth $1000$ m, advected by GLORYS daily $(u,v)$ over $15$–$50^\circ$ N, $70$–$30^\circ$ W. Floats advect continuously at park depth and record a position every $10$ days; there is no ascent, descent or surface drift, so a cycle is a position sample, not a simulated dive. Floats are deleted on leaving the velocity domain and retired at a lifespan drawn from the real Argo record for this region ($418$ deployments, median $\approx 1500$ d). **Estimation.** $\hat Z_k$ is the unweighted mean of $\tilde Z_k$ at the profile positions for year $k$, and $\bar Z_k$ is the exact $\mathbb{P}$-weighted domain mean of the same field for year $k$. # The analysis domain Two analysis boxes sit inside the downloaded GLORYS region, both spanning $60^\circ$–$40^\circ$ W: **Box B** ($35$–$45^\circ$ N) straddles the North Atlantic Current and the Gulf Stream extension, and **Box A** ($22$–$34^\circ$ N) has milder currents and OHC variability. Temperature was downloaded for the analysis boxes and a small buffer; velocity was downloaded over a larger region to advect floats, which are lost if they exit the velocity domain. ::: {#cell-fig-domain .cell execution_count=2} ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display} ![The two analysis boxes (filled) inside the downloaded GLORYS velocity and thetao regions (dashed).](osse_files/figure-html/fig-domain-output-1.png){#fig-domain width=821 height=716} ::: ::: ::: {#cell-fig-bathy .cell execution_count=3} ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display} ![GLORYS ocean depth over the advection domain (left) and the sub-2000 m cells excluded from the analysis (right), both boxes outlined.](osse_files/figure-html/fig-bathy-output-1.png){#fig-bathy width=1402 height=605} ::: ::: An analysis mask is placed on cells that must have temperature data for every depth level to $2000$m. Retained area is $92.35\%$ and $99.77\%$ for Box B and A respectively. The below figures show a single day's OHC anomaly and velocity fields for the analysis domain. A day was selected based on its percentile of spatial variability across cells for the given field over both analysis boxes. ::: {#cell-fig-days .cell execution_count=4} ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display} ![Residual field Z (GJ per m2) on days at the 5th, 50th and 95th percentile of the combined daily spatial dispersion, both boxes on one shared diverging scale.](osse_files/figure-html/fig-days-output-1.png){#fig-days width=1403 height=535} ::: ::: ::: {#cell-fig-vel-u .cell execution_count=5} ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display} ![Eastward velocity at 1000 m (cm/s), both boxes on one shared diverging scale.](osse_files/figure-html/fig-vel-u-output-1.png){#fig-vel-u width=1403 height=535} ::: ::: ::: {#cell-fig-vel-v .cell execution_count=6} ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display} ![Northward velocity at 1000 m (cm/s), both boxes on one shared diverging scale.](osse_files/figure-html/fig-vel-v-output-1.png){#fig-vel-v width=1403 height=535} ::: ::: **The flow is roughly twice as variable in Box B.** Median daily $\mathrm{sd}_{\mathbb{P}}$ is $12.1$ cm/s eastward and $11.5$ northward in Box B against $5.5$ and $5.4$ in Box A. Over 2010-2019, the range of daily spatial standard deviation in cm/s is $9.7$–$14.8$ (eastward) and $9.0$–$14.7$ (northward) in Box B, $4.5$–$7.0$ (eastward) and $4.4$–$6.7$ (northward) in Box A. # Mean field {#sec-meanfield} The sampling-bias question concerns the *residual anomaly* OHC field, not the total. We therefore decompose $$\mathrm{OHC}(c,t) \;=\; \hat m(c,t) \;+\; \tilde Z(c,t),$$ with $\hat m$ a mean field fitted per cell once across all years and $\tilde Z_k$ the year-$k$ residual the designs sample. **Regression.** For each analysis cell $c$, OHC is modelled as $\mathrm{OHC}(c,t) = \phi(t)^\top \beta_c + \varepsilon(c,t)$ on the trend-plus-harmonics basis $\phi(t) = \bigl(1,\,t,\,t^2,\,\sin 2\pi t,\,\cos 2\pi t,\,\sin 4\pi t,\,\cos 4\pi t\bigr)^\top$ ($t$ in decimal years): a quadratic trend and the annual and semiannual cycles. The coefficients are fit by least squares to the $1995$–$2019$ GLORYS *monthly* mean record. A GLORYS monthly file holds the month *mean* OHC over $I_m = [t_0^m, t_1^m)$ but is time-stamped at its start $t_0^m$. So we regress on the **window-averaged basis** $\bar\phi(I_m) = |I_m|^{-1}\!\int_{I_m}\phi(t)\,dt$, so the OHC monthly response and seasonal basis are monthly averages. The design matrix is $\bar X = \bigl[\bar\phi(I_m)^\top\bigr]_m$ and the per-cell fit is $\hat\beta_c = \bar X^{+} Y_c$. **Prediction is then pointwise:** the fitted field is evaluated at each instant on the daily grid, $\hat m(c,t) = \phi(t)^\top \hat\beta_c$, and subtracted from daily OHC to give $\tilde Z_k = \mathrm{OHC}_k - \hat m$ on the same mask. ::: {#cell-fig-meanfield .cell execution_count=7} ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display} ![Fitted mean field (quadratic trend plus annual and semiannual harmonics) at mid-month 2015, both boxes on one shared scale, in GJ per m2.](osse_files/figure-html/fig-meanfield-output-1.png){#fig-meanfield width=1484 height=472} ::: ::: ::: {#cell-fig-decomp3 .cell execution_count=8} ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display} ![The OHC = mean field + residual decomposition on one shared day, both boxes drawn per field, in GJ per m2.](osse_files/figure-html/fig-decomp3-output-1.png){#fig-decomp3 width=1469 height=681} ::: ::: ::: {#cell-fig-ohc-series .cell execution_count=9} ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display} ![Daily domain-mean OHC with the fitted mean field (top) and their difference, the domain-mean anomaly (bottom), per box over 2010-2019 in GJ per m2.](osse_files/figure-html/fig-ohc-series-output-1.png){#fig-ohc-series width=1199 height=704} ::: ::: # Estimand, truth, and estimator Let $\mathbb{P}$ be the normalized area $\times$ time probability measure over the depth masked analysis domain. The target is the residual field's domain mean, $$\bar Z_k \;=\; \int_{\mathcal{X}} \tilde Z_k \, d\mathbb{P},$$ for each analysis year $k$, where $\tilde Z_k$ is the year-$k$ OHC 0–2000 m field with the fitted mean field removed. A design is a finite point set $\{x_i\}_{i=1}^{n} \subset \mathcal{X}$ — the year-$k$ in-box profiles of one deployment realization $d$; its estimator and bias are $$\hat Z^{(d)}_k \;=\; \frac{1}{n}\sum_{i=1}^{n} \tilde Z_k\!\left(x_i^{(d)}\right), \qquad B^{(d)}_k \;=\; \hat Z^{(d)}_k - \bar Z_k .$$ $\tilde Z_k$ is a simple function on the native $1/12^\circ \times$ daily grid, so evaluating it at $x_i$ is the cell-day lookup of the *containing* cell. ::: {#80e61e99 .cell execution_count=10} ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=10} ```{=html}

The dispersion $\sigma_k = \mathrm{sd}_{\mathbb{P}}(\tilde Z_k)$ is $6.3$–$7.6$ GJ/m$^2$ in Box B and $1.7$–$2.4$ in Box A. # Deployment One continuous advection per realization generates the sampling. For realization $d$, $N$ floats are seeded uniformly over normalized spacetime across the velocity record of 2010-2019. Each realization therefore yields $B^{(d)}_k$ for every analysis year at once, flow and field the same calendar year. **How a float is advected.** Each float is carried by GLORYS12V1 daily horizontal velocity $(u,v)$ at a fixed park depth of $1000$ m and held there for its whole life — there is *no dive cycle*. The two archived velocity levels bracketing $1000$ m ($902$ and $1062$ m) are linearly interpolated to the park depth (as OceanParcels does natively), and the float is stepped forward at a $1$-hour time step. Its position is written every $10$ days, and that recorded park-depth position is taken as the profile — the point where a real float would begin its ascent — so a cycle is a position sample, not a simulated dive. A float is deleted when it leaves the velocity domain and retired at a lifespan drawn from the real Argo record (median $\approx 1500$ d). The pilot is **$100$ independent realizations**. Each seeds **$1{,}000$ floats** uniformly over normalized space–time on the ($\mathrm{deptho}\ge 1000$ m) region spanning both boxes plus an $8^\circ$ margin, across $2010\text{-}01\text{-}01$ to $2019\text{-}12\text{-}26$, and advects them once at $1000$ m park depth ($10$-day profiling cycle, lifespans drawn from the real Argo record). Years $2010$–$2014$ are the equilibration lead; bias is calculated on **$2015$–$2019$**. ::: {.panel-tabset} ### Simulated advection ::: {#cell-fig-advection .cell execution_count=11} ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display} ![One simulated deployment: 60 float drift tracks and their 10-day profile points coloured by year, only in-box profiles (filled) entering an estimate.](osse_files/figure-html/fig-advection-output-1.png){#fig-advection width=947 height=722} ::: ::: ### Real Argo ::: {#cell-fig-advection-argo .cell execution_count=12} ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display} ![Real Argo trajectories over the same domain and years (60 of 740 floats) coloured by year, on the same base map for comparison.](osse_files/figure-html/fig-advection-argo-output-1.png){#fig-advection-argo width=947 height=722} ::: ::: ::: **Real deployment geometry.** The map below shows the raw (not QC-cleaned) deployment position of every real Argo float first observed inside the advection domain over $2010$–$2019$ ($418$ floats), coloured by deployment year — the release geometry the real-deployment arms (below) seed from, and the starting point for the per-float bias-over-time analysis. Deployment is taken as each float's earliest profile on record, so a float first observed before the file window is not resolved here. ::: {#cell-fig-deploy-positions .cell execution_count=13} ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display} ![Raw Argo deployment positions in the advection domain, 2010-2019, coloured by deployment year, on the shared domain base map (dashed: velocity and thetao download regions; filled: the two analysis boxes).](osse_files/figure-html/fig-deploy-positions-output-1.png){#fig-deploy-positions width=947 height=722} ::: ::: ## A single deployment cluster {#sec-cluster} Six floats were deployed within a $\sim\!14$-hour window on $27$–$28$ September $2015$ in a tight cluster in the NW corner of Box B ($43.4$–$44.3^\circ$ N, $-55.8$ to $-57.8^\circ$ W), on the Grand Banks / Gulf Stream–Labrador confluence. They are a clean natural experiment in deployment geometry: a common release point and time, whose per-float sampling bias we can then follow profile by profile. For a single profile at position $x_i$ in year $k$, its bias as an estimate of the domain mean is $Z_k(x_i) - \bar Z_k$; the charts track that quantity along each float's life (in-box profiles only, where the residual field is defined), with the cluster mean over-plotted. The two tabs evaluate it at the *real* Argo positions and at the *GLORYS park-advection* sim-twin positions of the same floats, so their divergence is the same real-vs-reanalysis gap the trajectory maps show. ::: {.panel-tabset} ### Real Argo ::: {#cell-fig-cluster-bias .cell execution_count=14} ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display} ![Single-profile bias Z(x_i) - Zbar_k (GJ per m2) vs profile number for each of the six floats at their real Argo positions, with the cluster mean (black). Only in-box profiles carry a defined bias.](osse_files/figure-html/fig-cluster-bias-output-1.png){#fig-cluster-bias width=1198 height=539} ::: ::: ### GLORYS advection ::: {#cell-fig-cluster-bias-sim .cell execution_count=15} ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display} ![The same single-profile bias evaluated at the GLORYS 1000 m park-advection sim-twin positions of the six floats. In-box counts differ from the real tab because the park tracks drift out of the box on a different schedule.](osse_files/figure-html/fig-cluster-bias-sim-output-1.png){#fig-cluster-bias-sim width=1198 height=539} ::: ::: ::: The two trajectory maps below trace the same six floats (one colour each; deployment a star, last fix an open circle): the GLORYS park-advection sim twin against the real Argo path from the shared deployment. ::: {.panel-tabset} ### GLORYS advection ::: {#cell-fig-cluster-sim .cell execution_count=16} ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display} ![GLORYS 1000 m park-advection sim-twin trajectories of the six floats from their real deployment positions.](osse_files/figure-html/fig-cluster-sim-output-1.png){#fig-cluster-sim width=894 height=804} ::: ::: ### Real Argo ::: {#cell-fig-cluster-real .cell execution_count=17} ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display} ![Real Argo trajectories of the same six floats on the same base map.](osse_files/figure-html/fig-cluster-real-output-1.png){#fig-cluster-real width=894 height=804} ::: ::: ::: # The sampling weight field The bias $B^{(d)}_k = \langle \tilde Z_k,\, w^{(d)} - p\rangle$, the inner product of the residual field with the excess of the empirical sampling weight over the uniform weight p. One realization's sampling is the normalized empirical measure $$w^{(d)} \;=\; \frac{1}{n}\sum_{i=1}^{n} \delta_{x_i}$$ on the spacetime domain $\mathcal{X} = \mathcal{A} \times \mathcal{T}$. Averaging it over realizations gives $\mathbb{E}[w]$, the normalized occupancy (intensity) measure of the advective array, with $\mathbb{E}[B_k] = \langle \tilde Z_k,\, \mathbb{E}[w] - p\rangle$. We define the spatial marginal sampling weight as $$w^{\mathrm{sp}}_c \;=\; \sum_{\tau\in\mathcal{T}} w_{c,\tau} \;=\; \frac{\#\{\,i : x_i \in c\,\}}{n},$$ the fraction of a realization's profiles that fall in cell $c$, summed over all days. The maps below show $\mathbb{E}[w^{\mathrm{sp}}_c]$ — the expected such fraction, i.e. the array's normalized spatial intensity — over the years $2015$–$2019$ on the native $1/12^\circ$ grid, against the uniform area marginal $p^{\mathrm{sp}}_c = A_c / \sum_{c'} A_{c'}$, as the ratio $q_c = \mathbb{E}[w^{\mathrm{sp}}_c] / p^{\mathrm{sp}}_c$ ($=1$ under area-fair sampling). ## Spatial marginal ::: {#cell-fig-wspace .cell execution_count=18} ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display} ![Over- and under-sampling log2(E[w]/uniform) on the native 1/12 deg grid, both boxes on one map per scored year and one shared scale (red over-sampled, blue under, white uniform).](osse_files/figure-html/fig-wspace-output-1.png){#fig-wspace width=1677 height=417} ::: ::: The per-cell weight distribution about the uniform value of 1, one panel per year: ::: {.panel-tabset} ### Box B ::: {#cell-fig-whist .cell execution_count=19} ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display} ![Box B distribution of the per-cell weight E[w]/uniform over native cells per year, about the uniform value of 1 (red line).](osse_files/figure-html/fig-whist-output-1.png){#fig-whist width=1417 height=318} ::: ::: ### Box A ::: {#cell-fig-whist-a .cell execution_count=20} ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display} ![Box A distribution of the per-cell weight E[w]/uniform, same construction as Box B.](osse_files/figure-html/fig-whist-a-output-1.png){#fig-whist-a width=1417 height=318} ::: ::: ::: ## Bias as a covariance Let $q = w/p$ be the sampling frequency of each cell-day relative to its uniform share — the over/under-sampling factor mapped in @fig-wspace and distributed in @fig-whist, equal to $1$ under uniform sampling and with $\int q\,\mathrm{d}\mathbb{P} = 1$. The bias is the inner product of the field with the sampling excess, $$B_k \;=\; \langle \tilde Z_k,\, q - 1\rangle_{\mathbb{P}} \;=\; \langle \tilde Z_k - \bar Z_k,\, q - 1\rangle_{\mathbb{P}},$$ the second equality because $\langle 1, q-1\rangle_{\mathbb{P}} = 0$ — a spatially uniform field is sampled without bias. Cauchy–Schwarz for this inner product gives the cap $$|B_k| \;\le\; \lVert \tilde Z_k - \bar Z_k\rVert_{\mathbb{P}}\,\lVert q - 1\rVert_{\mathbb{P}} \;=\; \sigma_k \, \operatorname{sd}_{\mathbb{P}}(q),$$ with $\sigma_k = \operatorname{sd}_{\mathbb{P}}(\tilde Z_k)$ (the residual-field table) and $\operatorname{sd}_{\mathbb{P}}(q)$ the spread of the over/under-sampling factor (@fig-whist), attained only when $q-1$ is proportional to the field anomaly. **Zero bias does not require uniform sampling** — it requires only that $q - 1$ be orthogonal to $\tilde Z_k$ in $L^2(\mathbb{P})$; a strongly non-uniform array ($\operatorname{sd}_{\mathbb{P}}(q) \gg 0$) can still be unbiased for this functional. # Results ## Pilot specification Across all $100$ realizations the pilot seeds $10^5$ float-deployments and scores about $2.15$ million in-box profiles (the table below). Per realization, Box B holds $\sim\!90$ distinct floats (standing stock $\sim\!40$) giving $\sim\!1{,}410$–$1{,}490$ profiles a year; Box A holds $\sim\!145$ floats (stock $\sim\!78$) giving $\sim\!2{,}730$–$2{,}900$ — its quiescent flow retains more of the same deployment. ::: {#48c5eb04 .cell execution_count=22} ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=22} ```{=html}

Two experiments seed the *same* GLORYS park advection from the real Argo deployment record instead of uniformly in space–time, to separate how much of that gap is the *geometry* of where and when Argo is deployed from how much is real float motion diverging from the simplified advection. The pool is each cleaned float's first profile inside the box-plus-$8^\circ$ margin over $2010$–$2019$ ($359$ deployments, with their real positions, dates, and lifespans). **argo-actual** advects that set verbatim — one realization, the direct fidelity check; **argo-bootstrap** resamples it with replacement at the real rate ($100$ realizations), each drawn seed position perturbed by an independent Gaussian jitter of $5$ km standard deviation per axis (a few $1/12^\circ$ cells) so that repeated draws of the same real deployment are not exact duplicates, carrying the real deployment pattern with a Monte-Carlo spread. ::: {#21ffc932 .cell execution_count=30} ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=30} ```{=html}

So **roughly half of the real Box B bias is deployment geometry**: where and when Argo is actually put in the water, carried by the flow, lands profiles preferentially over cold anomalies, something uniform-in-space–time seeding does not reproduce. The remaining $\sim\!0.3$ GJ/m$^2$ is the residual the park-only advection cannot capture — real trajectories diverging from GLORYS (ascent/surface drift/descent, real currents $\neq$ reanalysis). The actual-deployment realization tracks the real sign and magnitude in $2015$–$2018$ but is one noisy draw ($2019$ swings to $+1.9$), and the real values sit within the bootstrap spread. Box A stays small under every deployment law. One caveat: the bootstrap's in-box standing stock ($\sim\!15$) is below real Argo's ($\sim\!27$–$30$) because the real array also draws floats deployed outside the seed region that drift in; in-box profile counts still match ($\sim\!500$/yr), so the $n$-independent mean-bias comparison holds. ## Is the residual gap the missing dive cycle? The park-only sim omits the dive cycle — the ascent, the $\sim\!1$-day surface drift, and the descent — so one reading of the residual $\sim\!0.3$ GJ/m$^2$ is that a profile recorded at the $1000$ m park position sits systematically away from where a real float actually surfaces. Each float is a matched colour pair -- real the darker solid line, sim twin the lighter dashed line: a Box A float in blue/cyan (~8 yr, subtropical gyre) and a Box B float in purple/pink (~6 yr, NAC / Gulf Stream).](osse_files/figure-html/fig-twins-output-1.png){#fig-twins width=920 height=804} ::: ::: The sim loses the real float fast: median separation is already $\sim\!53$ km at one $10$-day cycle, $\sim\!135$ km at a month and $\sim\!290$ km at three, climbing through $\sim\!590$ km at a year (@fig-divergence). The field's mesoscale correlation length is $\sim\!50$–$100$ km, so the GLORYS-park position exceeds it *within a single cycle* and is several correlation lengths off well inside the analysis year — it samples effectively independent locations at the seasonal scale that sets the bias. Individual twins make this concrete (@fig-twins): a subtropical-gyre float and its twin part slowly, while a NAC / Gulf-Stream float and its twin split early and end up in different parts of the basin. A dive cycle would add only the $\sim\!1$-day surface excursion per cycle (tens of km, largely non-persistent), far too small to produce or repair a divergence that grows at $\sim\!5$ km/day. **So the drift residual is reanalysis and advection error — real $1000$ m currents and unresolved eddies, not the missing surfacing — and adding a dive cycle to the advection would not close it.** (The $\pm 6$-day matching tolerance inflates the $10$-day point; the month-plus separations dwarf it, and the separation also bundles the surface-vs-park offset, which only reinforces the conclusion.) # Conclusions From this $100$-realization pilot: **The advective sampling bias is small but not zero.** In both boxes $\mathbb{E}[B_k]$ stays within $\sim\!0.02\,\sigma_k$ (the bias tables) — a few hundredths of a GJ/m$^2$ against a field varying by $6$–$8$ (Box B) and $2$ (Box A) GJ/m$^2$. It is not identically zero: several years are resolved at $2$–$4$ Monte-Carlo standard errors, so the array is weakly preferential in effect, at a magnitude that is a small fraction of the field's own variability. **Strong non-uniform sampling, nearly orthogonal to the field.** The array samples space genuinely non-uniformly (on-mask up to $\sim\!3.6\times$ over-sampling, $\operatorname{sd}_{\mathbb{P}}(q)\approx0.4$; @fig-whist), yet the bias is only $\sim\!1$–$5\%$ of the Cauchy–Schwarz ceiling that non-uniformity permits, i.e. a weight–field correlation $|\rho_k|\approx0.02$. Preferential sampling does not imply preferential bias for this functional — the estimand-level bias is the covariance $\operatorname{Cov}_{\mathbb{P}}(q,\tilde Z_k)$, and the array sits near its null space, not a property of sampling non-uniformity per se. **Both regimes are comparably biased once standardized.** Box B has larger raw bias and spread, but on the $\sigma_k$ scale the energetic western-boundary region is not disproportionately biased relative to the quiescent gyre.
